package.name: gbplanner_elevation_map
package.description:
A 2.5D elevation map built from the robot's point cloud, published as grid_map_msgs/GridMap on "elevation_map".
gbplanner's ground-robot mode (RobotParams.type kGroundRobot) projects every sample and every edge onto that layer: Rrg::projectSampleEleMap snaps a sample to the terrain height and refuses it if the robot's footprint corners are steeper than PlanningParams.max_inclination. On a real ANYmal the layer comes from ANYbotics' elevation_mapping. Nothing in gbplanner_ros publishes it, which is why upstream's own UGV demos ship RobotParams.type kAerialRobot: with no elevation layer projectSampleEleMap rejects every sample and the graph never leaves one vertex.
This node fills that gap for the simulation, so a ground robot can be planned for as one.
